sections.label: ICAO CORSIA implementation by CAAS
sections.summary: This enables CAAS to implement provisions relating to the ICAO Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, to enable CAAS to implement the provisions relating to the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA).

sections.label: Changi East development scale and cost
sections.summary: The Changi East development is unprecedented in scale and complexity and is expected to cost tens of billions of dollars.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Changi East development is unprecedented in scale and complexity and is expected to cost tens of billions of dollars.

sections.label: Airport charges and development levy
sections.summary: Airport users will contribute through aeronautical charges and a new Airport Development Levy applied to air tickets issued on or after 1 July 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Airport users will contribute through aeronautical charges and a new Airport Development Levy (ADL), which will be applied to air tickets issued on or after 1 July 2018.

sections.label: CADF funds and government injection
sections.summary: The Government set up the CADF in 2015 to hold funds for major airport developments and has injected $4 billion into it.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Government had set up the CADF in 2015 to hold funds for major airport developments and has, thus far, injected $4 billion into the CADF.

sections.label: Reserve fund and CAAS sanctions
sections.summary: Clause 15 requires the airport licensee to establish, maintain and contribute to a reserve fund, and clause 14 enables CAAS sanctions for failure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Accordingly, clause 15 sets out the requirement for the airport licensee to establish, maintain and contribute to a reserve fund.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Clause 14 enables CAAS to apply sanctions on the airport licensee, such as a financial penalty, in the event that it fails to set up, maintain or contribute to the reserve fund, or withdraws funds from the fund without CAAS' approval.

sections.label: Airport capacity management scheme
sections.summary: Clause 20 introduces a new airport capacity management scheme enabling stronger deterrent measures against slot misuse.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Clause 20 introduces a new airport capacity management scheme that enables stronger deterrent measures against slot misuse.

sections.label: Bill penalties for non-compliance
sections.summary: The Bill lets the slots coordinator impose regulatory sanctions and a maximum financial penalty of up to S$100,000 for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In the event of non-compliance, the Bill enables the slots coordinator to impose regulatory sanctions and a maximum financial penalty of up to S$100,000.

sections.label: Changi capacity and Jewel opening
sections.summary: Second Minister Ng said the 66 million passengers per annum capacity is almost fully used, and Jewel Changi Airport will raise it to 85 MPPA by 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second Minister Ng told us that we have almost fully utilised all the 66 million passengers per anuum (MPPA) capacity and by 2019 Jewel Changi Airport will open and bring the total capacity to 85 MPPA.

sections.label: Suvarnabhumi airport upgrade
sections.summary: Suvarnabhumi is set for a 117-billion baht upgrade through 2021 that will include a third runway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Suvarnabhumi is set for a 117-billion baht upgrade through 2021 which will include, like us, a third runway.

sections.label: Aviation emissions regulations and ICAO measures
sections.summary: Mr Ng cited 50 MPPA initially, and the Bill enables regulations for the Chicago Convention and other agreements on mitigating international aviation emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Ng cited 50 MPPA in its initial phase, so, the MPPA may possibly increase in subsequent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This Bill just proposed to enable the making of regulations to give effect to the Chicago Convention and any other international agreement to which Singapore is a party for mitigating specifically the environmental effect of international aviation emission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But even as ICAO have painstakingly agreed in recent years to take various mitigation measures to reduce aviation emissions, such as Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), our new aircraft CO2 emissions standards and so on, they alone may still be insufficient for various reasons, such as the non-application of emission regulations to older aircraft, given the relatively long lifespan of aircraft or the non-uniform application of regulations across different states.

sections.label: T5 pollution and noise questions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a 60% MPPA increase will bring noise pollution to eastern residents and seeks current and projected pollutant levels at Changi.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With the projected 60% increase in MPPA, will it bring new levels of noise pollution to residents living in the east and north-east, such as Changi, Loyang, Pasir Ris, Tampines, Tanah Merah, Bedok and East Coast?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One, what are the current levels of nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, sulphur oxides, particulate matter, volatile organic compounds or any other types of pollutants that are currently generated at Changi Airport as well as the projected levels of such pollutants which can be expected to be generated when T5 opens?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two, has the Government done any studies regarding the projected air and noise pollution that may come with the opening phase of T5 and, if so, when can the Government release the details of such studies?

sections.label: Airport pollution safeguard question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government intends air or noise pollution safeguards for people living within 10 km to 15 km of Changi Airport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Five, does the Government intend to introduce any air or noise pollution safeguards to protect people living within a certain distance from the airport, for example, say, a radius of 10 km to 15 km from Changi Airport and, if so, what are these measures?

sections.label: Airport Development Levy collection
sections.summary: The ADL forms part of airport users' share towards funding new Changi East developments, set at $10.80 for Origin-Destination and $3.00 for Transit/Transfer passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The first is the collection of the new Airport Development Levy (ADL), which would form part of airport users’ share towards funding the new Changi East developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Second Minister has explained why we would need an ADL during the MOT Committee of Supply and that the Government had arrived at the ADL quantum of $10.80 for Origin-Destination passengers and $3.00 for Transit/Transfer passengers after studying the funding models of other airports and consulting the industry in Singapore.

sections.label: Reserve fund from Changi profits
sections.summary: The Bill allows for the creation of a reserve fund from the Changi Airport Group's profits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The second policy is that this Bill allows for the creation of a reserve fund from the Changi Airport Group’s profits.

sections.label: Airport capacity management scheme
sections.summary: A major amendment introduces a new airport capacity management scheme to better optimise the use of airport capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The other major amendment in this Bill aims to better optimise the use of airport capacity, by introducing a new airport capacity management scheme.

sections.label: Revised ADL charges downwards
sections.summary: The initial proposal to collect $12 from Origin-Destination and $6 from Transit/Transfer passengers was revised downwards after industry consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For a fact, our initial proposal was to collect $12 from departing Origin-Destination passengers and $6 from departing Transit/Transfer passengers, but we had revised this downwards following our industry consultation.

sections.label: Short-term measures for airlines
sections.summary: There will not be a staggered implementation, but the Government will put in place short-term measures to assist airlines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: While there will not be a staggered implementation, the Government will put in place short-term measures to assist airlines.

sections.label: Slot abuse penalty and CORSIA
sections.summary: The maximum quantum of $100,000 would wipe out profits from abusing slots, and Singapore embarked on CORSIA voluntarily on air pollution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For example, the maximum quantum of $100,000 would wipe out any profits from abusing any slots to operate a flight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: On air pollution, I think this is why the Singapore Government has embarked on this Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) on a voluntary basis.

sections.label: Government car-lite position
sections.summary: The Government's position is to go car-lite, with car growth limited to zero.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: But, ultimately, the Government's position is to go car-lite.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We have limited the growth of cars and other vehicles and, for car growth, it is down to zero now.

sections.label: Third runway operations
sections.summary: The third runway is not new, and operations between the Singapore Airforce and the Civil Aviation Authority have been ongoing for many years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: The third runway is not a new runway and operations between the Singapore Airforce and the Civil Aviation Authority have been ongoing for many, many years.

sections.label: Runway Three military history
sections.summary: In Changi East, Runway Three used to be the military runway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In fact, in Changi East, Runway Three used to be the military runway.

sections.label: Bill supports air hub
sections.summary: The Bill will give levers to support the air hub in growing and remaining a success factor for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: With that, I think I have addressed most of the questions from Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: And, therefore, Mr Deputy Speaker, may I conclude that, with this Bill, we will have the levers to support the air hub in growing from strength to strength so that it continues to remain a success factor for Singapore and bring benefits for Singapore and Singaporeans.      .
